texts: good. the cold wind gets its own witness with 'cold' as a separate property, the blowing carries the sea as its source and night, day 16 and Year 1 as its time, and the wind is the undergoer rather than a doer, which is right for a natural force. one caveat no wording can dodge: 'day 16 of Year 1' lands on the ordinary day-of-month term, since there is no day-of-year carrier — a translator-side gap, not a loss of what you wrote.
good. the striking reuses the same wind as sentence 1, the Cliff Path is named and typed, and the night slot is carried; the wind is the doer here, which is correct for a transitive clause.

good. the coming reuses the wind, the first hard frost gets its own witness with its rank recorded, and the ordering 'wind before frost' is stated. the frost is left untensed, so the parse does not claim the frost itself happened — right for something that is only a time anchor.

bad: two things go wrong. 'Keepers' is a bare plural, i.e. indefinite, so the parse's placing of the group's typing and its 'on the Cliff Path' restrictor outside the denial is wrong — for an indefinite subject both belong inside the denied bundle — and the denial is also missing its per-keeper twin, which a distributive verb like 'add' owes. Making the set definite fixes the first and fits the passage, which has already established these keepers: 'The keepers on the Cliff Path had not yet added salt-bloom to the mire-essence, because the salt-bloom season had not started.' One thing wording cannot fix: 'because' joining two denied clauses records a reason relation between two events that did not happen, so if that causal link matters, state the cause positively in its own sentence (e.g. when the salt-bloom season does start).

mixed: the eleven lanterns, their count, the Middle Row and the per-lantern distribution are all carried, but the distributed conclusion drops the past tense — it says each lantern is unprepared, not was unprepared — which widens a state your sentence restricts to that night. nothing in your wording causes that, so no rewrite is strictly owed; if you want the time restriction stated rather than left to the reader, write 'That night, the eleven lanterns on the Middle Row were unprepared.'

good. 'went out' is kept whole as one phrasal symbol, the lanterns are the same eleven from sentence 5, 'before dawn' becomes an at-most-dawn bound, and the group event is paired with a fireable per-lantern rule so a named lantern can inherit it.

good. 'no lantern at the Sunken Cove' becomes a fireable strength-0 rule over lanterns at the cove, with the quantifier word recorded and the cove named and typed. (one translator-side caveat: this rule and sentence 6's share the same per-member event name, so the two would collide if those lantern sets ever overlapped — nothing your wording can change.)

good. same shape as sentence 7 and equally fireable. unlike the Sunken Cove, the Northcove gets no 'cove' type atom, because its kind word is fused into the name instead of standing as a separate word — a known gap in the naming rules, not a loss of anything your sentence states.

bad: the parse treats 'the north wind' as the very cold wind of sentence 1 and asserts that wind is a north wind, which your text never says. the sheltering itself, the cliff-spires as a counted group and the Northcove as what is sheltered are all fine. say which wind you mean: 'The cliff-spires sheltered the Northcove against that cold wind.' if it is the wind of sentence 1, or 'The cliff-spires sheltered the Northcove against a north wind.' if it is a different one.
